summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: algorithm analysis with big-O, divide and conquer and sorting, discrete mathematics (sets, permutations, modular arithmetic, primes, induction), and introductory linear algebra (matrices, linear maps, invertibility, triangular and permutation matrices). They know polynomials and complex numbers including roots of unity and Euler's formula, basic calculus functions, and basic Turing machines with several tapes and head movements. They have probably met schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication and the idea of the FFT, but have not studied abstract algebra beyond basics, finite-field theory, numerical analysis of error, multidimensional Fourier methods, or the Schönhage–Strassen line of fast multiplication.

known.name: Binary numerals and bit strings
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written in base 2 as a string of bits, with value the sum of bit times power of two, and a fixed-width string may be padded with leading zeros.

known.name: Positional notation in any radix
known.gloss: An integer is written as a sum of digits times powers of a base, and digit lists of different bases or mixed bases are converted by repeated division with remainder.

known.name: Integer division with remainder, floor and ceiling
known.gloss: For integers a and b>0 there are unique q=floor(a/b) and r with a=bq+r and 0<=r<b, and floor, ceiling and rounding map reals to nearby integers.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Integers are compared and added or multiplied after reduction modulo m, so that wrap-around of an index or a value modulo m is well defined.

known.name: Arithmetic modulo 2 and XOR
known.gloss: Bitwise exclusive-or is addition of bits modulo 2, so x XOR x = 0 and a XOR b XOR b = a, which allows undoing an added value.

known.name: Primes, coprimality and gcd
known.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself, two integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1, and the gcd is found by Euclid's algorithm.

known.name: Roots of unity and Euler's formula
known.gloss: The complex number e^{2 pi i/t} satisfies z^t=1, has modulus 1, and its powers are the t-th roots of unity equally spaced on the unit circle.

known.name: Exponential, logarithm and Gaussian function
known.gloss: The functions 2^x, e^x and log with their identities, and the Gaussian e^{-x^2} as a rapidly decaying positive bump function, are standard calculus material.

known.name: Asymptotic notation beyond big-O
known.gloss: Omega gives asymptotic lower bounds, Theta two-sided bounds, and o(g) means the ratio to g tends to 0, with liminf the smallest limit point of a sequence.

known.name: Geometric series and sums
known.gloss: A sum of terms with constant ratio q<1 is bounded by the first term over 1-q, so geometrically decreasing costs add up to a constant multiple of the largest.

known.name: Divide and conquer and recurrences
known.gloss: A problem solved by recursive calls on smaller pieces has its cost described by a recurrence whose solution is found by unrolling or the master theorem.

known.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: Long multiplication of n-digit integers costs O(n^2) digit operations and Karatsuba's divide and conquer reduces this to O(n^1.585).

known.name: Sorting and its cost
known.gloss: Arrays of n items can be sorted in O(n log n) comparisons or steps by merge sort, so rearranging by a known key is a standard operation.

known.name: Permutations and bijections
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijective reordering of a finite list, composed and inverted as a function, and an involution or a swap is a permutation.

known.name: Sets, subsets and Cartesian products
known.gloss: Finite sets, their subsets, intersections and sizes, product sets of tuples, and the 0/1 indicator vector of a subset are basic discrete mathematics.

known.name: Multidimensional arrays and row-major order
known.gloss: A multidimensional array indexed by tuples is flattened into one list in lexicographic (row-major) order, with the last index varying fastest.

known.name: Matrices, vectors and linear maps
known.gloss: Vectors and matrices over the reals, rationals or complex numbers, linear maps as matrix multiplication, composition as matrix product, invertibility and linear combinations.

known.name: Triangular and permutation matrices
known.gloss: Triangular matrices vanish on one side of the diagonal, a permutation matrix has a single 1 in each row and column, and matrices can be factored into such pieces by elimination.

known.name: Dot product, inner product and orthogonality
known.gloss: The dot product of two vectors is the sum of coordinate products, and vectors are orthogonal when it is zero.

known.name: Dyadic rationals and fixed-width numerators
aliases: number over a power of two
known.gloss: A dyadic rational has the form k/2^p with integer k, written in binary with p digits after the point, and sums and products of dyadics remain dyadic.

known.name: Matrix transposition
known.gloss: The transpose of a matrix swaps rows and columns, entry (i,j) becoming entry (j,i).

known.name: Triangle inequality and norms
known.gloss: The absolute value or modulus of a sum is at most the sum of the moduli, and a norm of a vector such as the maximum modulus of its entries obeys the same inequality.

known.name: Mathematical induction and proof by contradiction
known.gloss: Statements about all natural numbers are proved by a base case and an inductive step, which is standard proof technique for undergraduate computer science.

known.name: Cyclic shifts and rotations of lists
known.gloss: A cyclic shift by k moves entry i of a list of length S to position (i+k) mod S.

known.name: Subroutines and composition of algorithms
known.gloss: An algorithm may call another as a subroutine, with costs adding, and a problem is reduced to another by transforming inputs and outputs.
